## `GET /products`

**List Products**

Returns a paginated list of products. Omit `account_id` to search the public marketplace.

`operationId`: `listProducts` · tags: `Products` · seguridad: `bearerAuth`

### Parámetros

- **Api-Version-Date** (`header`) `string` — Pins the request to a dated API version.
- **account_id** (`query`) `string` — The unique identifier of the account to list products for. Omit to search the public marketplace.
- **query** (`query`) `string` — Ranked search against product title and headline. Omit to browse by recency.
- **marketplace_category_route** (`query`) `string` — Only return marketplace products assigned to this category route, such as `trading`.
- **plan_types** (`query`) `string[]` — Filter to products with a buyable plan of these billing models, such as `one_time` or `renewal`.
- **price_minimum** (`query`) `number` — Only return products whose advertised buyable plan has a displayed price of at least this amount. Recurring plans use renewal price.
- **price_maximum** (`query`) `number` — Only return products whose advertised buyable plan has a displayed price of at most this amount. Recurring plans use renewal price.
- **visibilities** (`query`) `string[]` — Filter to only products matching these visibility states. Ignored on the public marketplace list, which only returns visible products.
- **access_pass_types** (`query`) `string[]` — Filter to only products matching these types.
- **labels** (`query`) `string[]` — Filter to only products carrying all of these labels. Labels are matched lowercased.
- **direction** (`query`) `string` — The sort direction for results. Defaults to descending. · valores: `asc`, `desc`
- **order** (`query`) `string` — The field to sort results by. Account lists default to `created_at`. Marketplace lists default to `discoverable_at` and accept `created_at` or `discoverable_at`. Cannot be combined with `query`.
- **first** (`query`) `integer` — The number of products to return (default and max 100).
- **after** (`query`) `string` — A cursor; returns products after this position.
- **last** (`query`) `integer` — The number of products to return from the end of the range.
- **before** (`query`) `string` — A cursor; returns products before this position.
- **created_after** (`query`) `string` — Only return products created after this ISO 8601 timestamp.
- **created_before** (`query`) `string` — Only return products created before this ISO 8601 timestamp.

### Respuestas

**`200`** — marketplace products listed without an account

- **data** `ProductListItem[]` _requerido_
  - `array` de:
    - **account** `object | null` _requerido_ — Account that sells this product.
    - **created_at** `string` _requerido_ — When the product was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.
    - **default_plan** `ProductPublicPlan | null` _requerido_ — Buyable plan to show and check out with. The configured default when that plan is buyable, otherwise the first buyable plan in product-page order. `null` when none is buyable.
      - _uno de:_
        - **ProductPublicPlan**
          - **billing_period** `number | null` _requerido_ — Number of days between recurring charges, such as 30 for monthly or 365 for annual. `null` for one-time plans.
          - **expiration_days** `number | null` _requerido_ — Access duration in days for expiration-based plans. `null` for plans without an expiration.
          - **id** `string` _requerido_ — Plan ID, prefixed `plan_`.
          - **initial_price** `Money` _requerido_ — What checkout charges up front. `amount` is `"0.00"` when the first charge is free, such as a trial.
            - **amount** `string` _requerido_ — The amount in major units, as an exact decimal string — `"10.00"` is ten dollars. A string so no float rounds it in transit.
            - **currency** `string` _requerido_ — Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code, lowercase.
            - **decimals** `integer` _requerido_ — How many decimal places the amount CARRIES — the precision the charge itself runs at.
            - **display_decimals** `integer` _requerido_ — How many decimal places to SHOW. Usually equal to `decimals`, and deliberately not always: COP is charged in centavos but written in whole pesos, so it is `2` and `0`. Format the number in your own locale using this.
          - **plan_type** `string` _requerido_ — Billing model for this plan: `one_time` or `renewal`. · valores: `renewal`, `one_time`
          - **renewal_price** `Money` _requerido_ — The recurring charge every `billing_period` days. `amount` is `"0.00"` for one-time plans.
            - **amount** `string` _requerido_ — The amount in major units, as an exact decimal string — `"10.00"` is ten dollars. A string so no float rounds it in transit.
            - **currency** `string` _requerido_ — Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code, lowercase.
            - **decimals** `integer` _requerido_ — How many decimal places the amount CARRIES — the precision the charge itself runs at.
            - **display_decimals** `integer` _requerido_ — How many decimal places to SHOW. Usually equal to `decimals`, and deliberately not always: COP is charged in centavos but written in whole pesos, so it is `2` and `0`. Format the number in your own locale using this.
          - **title** `string | null` _requerido_ — Plan display name shown to customers. `null` if no title has been set.
          - **unlimited_stock** `boolean` _requerido_ — Whether the plan has unlimited stock.
          - **visibility** `string` _requerido_ — Where this plan can be seen. `visible` plans appear on the product page. · valores: `visible`, `hidden`, `archived`, `quick_link`
        - **null**
    - **description** `string | null` _requerido_ — Written description displayed on the product page. `null` if none is set.
    - **external_identifier** `string | null` _requerido_ — External identifier stored on the product for your own reference.
    - **gallery_images** `ProductGalleryImage[]` _requerido_
      - `array` de:
        - **content_type** `string | null` _requerido_ — Uploaded file MIME type, such as image/jpeg.
        - **id** `string` _requerido_ — Gallery image ID.
        - **url** `string | null` _requerido_ — Pre-optimized URL for rendering this image on the client.
    - **headline** `string | null` _requerido_ — Short marketing headline displayed on product page.
    - **id** `string` _requerido_ — Product ID, prefixed `prod_`.
    - **labels** `string[]` _requerido_
      - `array` de:
        - Lowercased labels used to group products into collections. Filter the list endpoint by `labels` to fetch one collection.
    - **member_count** `number` _requerido_ — Active memberships for this product; 0 if public member counts are disabled.
    - **metadata** `object | null` _requerido_ — Custom key-value pairs stored on the product.
    - **published_reviews_count** `number` _requerido_ — Published customer reviews for this product.
    - **route** `string` _requerido_ — URL slug for the product's public link.
    - **title** `string` _requerido_ — Product display name shown to customers.
    - **updated_at** `string` _requerido_ — When the product was last updated, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.
    - **verified** `boolean` _requerido_ — Whether the product has been verified by Whop.
    - **visibility** `string | null` _requerido_ — Whether the product is publicly visible, hidden, or archived.
- **page_info** `object` _requerido_
  - **end_cursor** `string | null` _requerido_
  - **has_next_page** `boolean` _requerido_
  - **has_previous_page** `boolean` _requerido_
  - **start_cursor** `string | null` _requerido_

**`400`** — Invalid Parameters

- **error** `object` _requerido_
  - **code** `string` — Machine-readable reason for this specific refusal, such as `bank_warning_not_acknowledged`. Only present when the error carries one.
  - **message** `string` _requerido_ — Human-readable error message.
  - **type** `string` _requerido_ — Machine-readable error code.

**`401`** — Unauthorized

- **error** `object` _requerido_
  - **code** `string` — Machine-readable reason for this specific refusal, such as `bank_warning_not_acknowledged`. Only present when the error carries one.
  - **message** `string` _requerido_ — Human-readable error message.
  - **type** `string` _requerido_ — Machine-readable error code.

- **global_affiliate_status** `string` — The enrollment status in the global affiliate program. · valores: `enabled`, `disabled`

**Update Product**

Updates an existing product.

`operationId`: `updateProduct` · tags: `Products` · seguridad: `bearerAuth`

### Parámetros

- **Api-Version-Date** (`header`) `string` — Pins the request to a dated API version.

- **banner_image** `object | null` — A wide image for the product, shown on the product page and on listing cards. Pass `{ id }` for an existing attachment or `{ direct_upload_id }` for a completed direct upload; `null` removes it.
  - **direct_upload_id** `string` — The signed id of a completed direct upload.
  - **id** `string` — The tag of an already-uploaded attachment.
- **description** `string | null` — A written description displayed on the product page.
- **headline** `string | null` — A short marketing headline for the product page.
- **labels** `array | null` — Labels used to group products into collections. Replaces the existing labels. Send an empty array to clear them.
  - `array` de:
- **metadata** `object | null` — Custom key-value pairs to store on the product.
- **product_tax_code_id** `string | null` — The unique identifier of the tax classification code. See the available [product categories](https://docs.numeral.com/essentials/product-categories).

- **title** `string` — The display name of the product.

## `GET /recommended_actions`

**List Action Chains**

Lists the recommended action chains for an account — short sequences of actions (create a product, price it, publish it) the account should run next, gated on what it already has.

`operationId`: `listRecommendedActions` · tags: `Recommended Actions` · seguridad: `bearerAuth`

### Parámetros

- **Api-Version-Date** (`header`) `string` — Pins the request to a dated API version.
- **account_id** (`query`) `string` — Account ID, prefixed `biz_`. Defaults to the API key's own account.

### Respuestas

**`200`** — defaults to the API key's own account

- **data** `AccountRecommendedActionChain[]` _requerido_
  - `array` de:
    - **actions** `AccountRecommendedActionChainStep[]` _requerido_
      - `array` de:
        - **action** `string` _requerido_ — The action definition key this step runs; new values may be added, so handle unknown actions gracefully
        - **cta** `string` _requerido_ — The URL where this step is done by hand
        - **cta_label** `string` _requerido_ — Button label
        - **description** `string` _requerido_ — Supporting copy, or empty
        - **error** `string | null` _requerido_ — Why the step failed, or `null`
        - **execution_type** `string` _requerido_ — Whether the client should navigate to the CTA or open the programmatic execution dialog · valores: `redirect`, `programatic`
        - **input** `object | null` _requerido_ — The filled-in request body for the step's endpoint, or `null` when it was not recorded
        - **output** `object | null` _requerido_ — The API response the step produced, or `null` until it succeeds
        - **position** `integer` _requerido_ — Zero-based order of this step within the chain
        - **reasoning** `object | null` _requerido_ — Why this step was recommended, or `null` when unavailable
        - **status** `string | null` _requerido_ — Where the run step currently stands, or `null` when the chain has not been run · valores: `pending`, `redirected`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `None`
        - **title** `string` _requerido_ — Headline for the step
    - **description** `string` _requerido_ — What running the chain accomplishes
    - **id** `string` _requerido_ — Chain ID — `rac_seed_<chain>_<nonce>` for seeded chains, `rac_chain_*` for generated ones
    - **reasoning** `object | null` _requerido_ — Why this chain was recommended, or `null` when unavailable
    - **title** `string` _requerido_ — Headline for the chain

**`401`** — Unauthorized

- **error** `object` _requerido_
  - **code** `string` — Machine-readable reason for this specific refusal, such as `bank_warning_not_acknowledged`. Only present when the error carries one.

## `GET /recommended_actions/{id}`

**Retrieve Action Chain**

Retrieves a recommended action chain by id, including chains that have already been run. Seeded chains are reconstructed from their hard-coded chain; generated chains are read from the account's stored chain, with each step's filled-in input.

`operationId`: `retrieveRecommendedAction` · tags: `Recommended Actions` · seguridad: `bearerAuth`

### Parámetros

- **Api-Version-Date** (`header`) `string` — Pins the request to a dated API version.
- **id** (`path`) `string` _requerido_ — Chain ID from the list endpoint, e.g. `rac_seed_start_selling_9f2c1a7b04`.
- **account_id** (`query`) `string` — Account ID, prefixed `biz_`. Defaults to the API key's own account.

### Respuestas

**`200`** — generated chain retrieved

- **actions** `AccountRecommendedActionChainStep[]` _requerido_
  - `array` de:
    - **action** `string` _requerido_ — The action definition key this step runs; new values may be added, so handle unknown actions gracefully
    - **cta** `string` _requerido_ — The URL where this step is done by hand
    - **cta_label** `string` _requerido_ — Button label
    - **description** `string` _requerido_ — Supporting copy, or empty
    - **error** `string | null` _requerido_ — Why the step failed, or `null`
    - **execution_type** `string` _requerido_ — Whether the client should navigate to the CTA or open the programmatic execution dialog · valores: `redirect`, `programatic`
    - **input** `object | null` _requerido_ — The filled-in request body for the step's endpoint, or `null` when it was not recorded
    - **output** `object | null` _requerido_ — The API response the step produced, or `null` until it succeeds
    - **position** `integer` _requerido_ — Zero-based order of this step within the chain
    - **reasoning** `object | null` _requerido_ — Why this step was recommended, or `null` when unavailable
    - **status** `string | null` _requerido_ — Where the run step currently stands, or `null` when the chain has not been run · valores: `pending`, `redirected`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `None`
    - **title** `string` _requerido_ — Headline for the step
- **description** `string` _requerido_ — What running the chain accomplishes
- **id** `string` _requerido_ — Chain ID — `rac_seed_<chain>_<nonce>` for seeded chains, `rac_chain_*` for generated ones

## `GET /resolution_center_cases`

**List Resolution Center Cases**

Lists resolution center cases. Without `account_id` you get every case you can read — the ones you opened as a buyer and every account you are a team member of; the filters narrow that list.

`operationId`: `listResolutionCenterCases` · tags: `Resolution Center Cases` · seguridad: `bearerAuth`

### Parámetros

- **Api-Version-Date** (`header`) `string` — Pins the request to a dated API version.
- **account_id** (`query`) `string` — Only cases filed against this account (`biz_` tag). With read access to the account this lists its whole queue; without, only the cases you opened against it.
- **user_id** (`query`) `string` — Only cases opened by this customer — a `user_` tag, or `me` for the calling user. It narrows what you can already read, so `me` lists the cases you opened without the ones on accounts you are a team member of.
- **first** (`query`) `integer` — The number of cases to return (default 20, max 100).
- **after** (`query`) `string` — A cursor; returns cases after this position.
- **last** (`query`) `integer` — The number of cases to return from the end of the range.
- **before** (`query`) `string` — A cursor; returns cases before this position.
- **order** (`query`) `string` — The field to sort cases by. · valores: `created_at`, `response_due_at` · default: `created_at`
- **direction** (`query`) `string` — Sort direction. · valores: `asc`, `desc` · default: `desc`
- **status** (`query`) `string[]` — Only cases in these statuses. Repeat the parameter to pass several — one paginated list covers all of them.
- **reason** (`query`) `string[]` — Only cases opened for these reasons. Repeat the parameter to pass several.
- **outcome** (`query`) `string[]` — Only closed cases that ended these ways. Repeat the parameter to pass several.
- **created_before** (`query`) `string` — Only cases created before this ISO 8601 timestamp.
- **created_after** (`query`) `string` — Only cases created after this ISO 8601 timestamp.

### Respuestas

**`200`** — cases listed

- **data** `ResolutionCenterCase[]` _requerido_
  - `array` de:
    - **account** `AccountSummary | null` _requerido_ — The account the case was filed against.
      - _uno de:_
        - **AccountSummary**
          - **id** `string` _requerido_ — Account ID, prefixed `biz_`.
          - **title** `string` _requerido_ — Account display name.
        - **null**
    - **amount** `number` _requerido_ — The amount in question, in whole units of `currency`.
    - **available_actions** `string[]` _requerido_
      - `array` de:
        - What you can do to this case right now, named for the endpoint that does it. Resolved for the calling credential, so a merchant and a customer reading the same case see their own options.
    - **buyer** `ResolutionBuyer` _requerido_ — The customer who opened the case.
      - **email** `string | null` _requerido_ — The customer's email address. Requires the `member:email:read` scope; `null` without it.
      - **member_id** `string | null` _requerido_ — The customer's member row on the account, prefixed `mem_`.
      - **name** `string | null` _requerido_ — The customer's display name.
      - **user_id** `string | null` _requerido_ — The customer's user ID, prefixed `user_`.
      - **username** `string | null` _requerido_ — The customer's Whop username.
    - **created_at** `string` _requerido_ — When the case was opened, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.
    - **currency** `string | null` _requerido_ — Three-letter ISO currency code of the amount.
    - **customer_appealed** `boolean` _requerido_ — Whether the customer has appealed a decision on this case.
    - **escalated** `boolean` _requerido_ — Whether Whop is involved — either reviewing the case, or waiting on the side named by `status` for something it asked for while reviewing.
    - **id** `string` _requerido_ — Resolution center case ID, prefixed `reso_`.
    - **outcome** `string | null` _requerido_ — Who prevailed on the claim. `null` until the case closes. Read `refund` for whether any money actually moved. · valores: `customer_won`, `merchant_won`, `withdrawn`, `None`
    - **payment** `ResolutionPayment` _requerido_ — The payment the case was opened against.
      - **card_brand** `string | null` _requerido_ — Card brand, when the customer paid by card.
      - **card_last4** `string | null` _requerido_ — Last four digits of the card, when the customer paid by card.
      - **created_at** `string` _requerido_ — When the payment was made, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.
      - **id** `string` _requerido_ — Payment ID, prefixed `pay_`.
      - **payment_method_type** `string | null` _requerido_ — How the customer paid, such as `card` or `paypal`.
    - **plan_id** `string | null` _requerido_ — The plan the payment was made on, prefixed `plan_`.
    - **product_id** `string | null` _requerido_ — The product the payment was for, prefixed `prod_`.
    - **reason** `string` _requerido_ — What the customer says went wrong. Shares the `/disputes` vocabulary, so a case that later becomes a chargeback reports the same complaint. · valores: `fraudulent`, `product_not_received`, `not_as_described`, `product_unacceptable`, `subscription_canceled`
    - **refund** `string | null` _requerido_ — Whether money moved and off whose balance: `none`, `merchant`, or `platform` (Whop refunded the customer and the merchant kept the funds). Independent of `outcome` — a case the merchant won can still carry a platform refund. `null` while the case is open, and on older closed cases that predate this being recorded. · valores: `none`, `merchant`, `platform`, `None`
    - **response_due_at** `string | null` _requerido_ — When the next response is due, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.
    - **status** `string` _requerido_ — Who the case is waiting on. `awaiting_merchant` and `awaiting_customer` name the side that owes a response, `under_review` means Whop is deciding, and `closed` means it is settled — read `outcome` for how. · valores: `awaiting_merchant`, `awaiting_customer`, `under_review`, `closed`
    - **updated_at** `string` _requerido_ — When the case was last changed, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.
- **page_info** `object` _requerido_
  - **end_cursor** `string | null` _requerido_
  - **has_next_page** `boolean` _requerido_
  - **has_previous_page** `boolean` _requerido_
  - **start_cursor** `string | null` _requerido_

**`401`** — Unauthorized

- **error** `object` _requerido_
  - **code** `string` — Machine-readable reason for this specific refusal, such as `bank_warning_not_acknowledged`. Only present when the error carries one.
  - **message** `string` _requerido_ — Human-readable error message.
  - **type** `string` _requerido_ — Machine-readable error code.

**`403`** — Forbidden

- **error** `object` _requerido_
  - **code** `string` — Machine-readable reason for this specific refusal, such as `bank_warning_not_acknowledged`. Only present when the error carries one.
  - **message** `string` _requerido_ — Human-readable error message.
  - **type** `string` _requerido_ — Machine-readable error code.

**`404`** — Resource not found

- **error** `object` _requerido_
  - **code** `string` — Machine-readable reason for this specific refusal, such as `bank_warning_not_acknowledged`. Only present when the error carries one.
  - **message** `string` _requerido_ — Human-readable error message.

## `GET /resolution_center_cases/summary`

**Retrieve Resolution Center Case Summary**

Aggregates the same cases `GET /resolution_center_cases` lists, using the same filters. Use it to build status tabs and issue filters without paging the whole list.

`operationId`: `retrieveResolutionCenterCaseSummary` · tags: `Resolution Center Cases` · seguridad: `bearerAuth`

### Parámetros

- **Api-Version-Date** (`header`) `string` — Pins the request to a dated API version.
- **groups** (`query`) `string[]` — Which breakdowns to return, keyed by these names under `groups`. Repeat the parameter to ask for several; omit it for all of them.
- **account_id** (`query`) `string` — The account to summarize cases for (`biz_` tag).
- **user_id** (`query`) `string` — Only cases opened by this customer — a `user_` tag, or `me` for the calling user.
- **status** (`query`) `string[]` — Only cases in these statuses.
- **reason** (`query`) `string[]` — Only cases opened for these reasons.
- **outcome** (`query`) `string[]` — Only closed cases that ended these ways.
- **created_before** (`query`) `string` — Only count cases created before this ISO 8601 timestamp.
- **created_after** (`query`) `string` — Only count cases created after this ISO 8601 timestamp.

### Respuestas

**`200`** — summary returned

- **groups** `object` _requerido_ — One entry per requested breakdown, keyed by the field it groups on. A field you did not ask for is absent.
  - **outcome** `object` — How many of the matching cases ended each way. Every outcome is present, including those with a count of zero; open cases are counted in none of them.
    - **customer_won** `integer` _requerido_
    - **merchant_won** `integer` _requerido_
    - **withdrawn** `integer` _requerido_
  - **reason** `object` — How many of the matching cases were opened for each reason. Every reason is present, including those with a count of zero.
    - **fraudulent** `integer` _requerido_
    - **not_as_described** `integer` _requerido_
    - **product_not_received** `integer` _requerido_
    - **product_unacceptable** `integer` _requerido_
    - **subscription_canceled** `integer` _requerido_
  - **status** `object` — How many of the matching cases are in each status. Every status is present, including those with a count of zero.
    - **awaiting_customer** `integer` _requerido_
    - **awaiting_merchant** `integer` _requerido_
    - **closed** `integer` _requerido_
    - **under_review** `integer` _requerido_
- **total** `integer` _requerido_ — How many cases match the filters.

**`400`** — Invalid Parameters

- **error** `object` _requerido_
  - **code** `string` — Machine-readable reason for this specific refusal, such as `bank_warning_not_acknowledged`. Only present when the error carries one.
  - **message** `string` _requerido_ — Human-readable error message.
  - **type** `string` _requerido_ — Machine-readable error code.

- **error** `object` _requerido_

## `GET /resolution_center_cases/{id}/events`

**List Resolution Center Case Events**

Lists the case timeline, newest first. Events the viewer is not allowed to see are omitted — a customer reads the customer-visible timeline, the merchant reads the full one.

`operationId`: `listResolutionCenterCaseEvents` · tags: `Resolution Center Cases` · seguridad: `bearerAuth`

### Parámetros

- **id** (`path`) `string` _requerido_ — The resolution center case ID (`reso_` tag).
- **Api-Version-Date** (`header`) `string` — Pins the request to a dated API version.
- **first** (`query`) `integer` — The number of events to return (default 20, max 100).
- **after** (`query`) `string` — A cursor; returns events after this position.
- **last** (`query`) `integer` — The number of events to return from the end of the range.
- **before** (`query`) `string` — A cursor; returns events before this position.

### Respuestas

**`200`** — events listed

- **data** `ResolutionEvent[]` _requerido_
  - `array` de:
    - **action** `string` _requerido_ — The action recorded in this event. · valores: `created`, `responded`, `accepted`, `denied`, `appealed`, `withdrew`, `requested_more_info`, `escalated`, `dispute_opened`, `dispute_customer_won`, `dispute_merchant_won`
    - **attachments** `ResolutionAttachment[]` _requerido_
      - `array` de:
        - **content_type** `string | null` _requerido_ — The file's MIME type.
        - **filename** `string | null` _requerido_ — The original file name.
        - **id** `string` _requerido_ — Unique identifier for the attachment, prefixed `att_`.
        - **url** `string | null` _requerido_ — A URL to view or download the file.
    - **created_at** `string` _requerido_ — When the event occurred, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.
    - **details** `string | null` _requerido_ — The message body or additional context provided with the event.
    - **id** `string` _requerido_ — Unique identifier for the event, prefixed `revt_`.
    - **reporter_type** `string` _requerido_ — The party that performed the action. · valores: `merchant`, `customer`, `platform`, `system`
    - **viewable_by_customer** `boolean` _requerido_ — Whether the customer can see this event in the timeline.
    - **viewable_by_merchant** `boolean` _requerido_ — Whether the merchant can see this event in the timeline.
- **page_info** `object` _requerido_
  - **end_cursor** `string | null` _requerido_
  - **has_next_page** `boolean` _requerido_
  - **has_previous_page** `boolean` _requerido_
  - **start_cursor** `string | null` _requerido_

**`401`** — Unauthorized

- **error** `object` _requerido_
  - **code** `string` — Machine-readable reason for this specific refusal, such as `bank_warning_not_acknowledged`. Only present when the error carries one.
  - **message** `string` _requerido_ — Human-readable error message.
  - **type** `string` _requerido_ — Machine-readable error code.

**`404`** — Resource not found

- **error** `object` _requerido_

- **created_at** `string` _requerido_ — When the case was opened, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.
- **currency** `string | null` _requerido_ — Three-letter ISO currency code of the amount.
- **customer_appealed** `boolean` _requerido_ — Whether the customer has appealed a decision on this case.
- **escalated** `boolean` _requerido_ — Whether Whop is involved — either reviewing the case, or waiting on the side named by `status` for something it asked for while reviewing.
- **id** `string` _requerido_ — Resolution center case ID, prefixed `reso_`.
- **outcome** `string | null` _requerido_ — Who prevailed on the claim. `null` until the case closes. Read `refund` for whether any money actually moved. · valores: `customer_won`, `merchant_won`, `withdrawn`, `None`
- **payment** `ResolutionPayment` _requerido_ — The payment the case was opened against.
  - **card_brand** `string | null` _requerido_ — Card brand, when the customer paid by card.
  - **card_last4** `string | null` _requerido_ — Last four digits of the card, when the customer paid by card.
  - **created_at** `string` _requerido_ — When the payment was made, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.
  - **id** `string` _requerido_ — Payment ID, prefixed `pay_`.
  - **payment_method_type** `string | null` _requerido_ — How the customer paid, such as `card` or `paypal`.
- **plan_id** `string | null` _requerido_ — The plan the payment was made on, prefixed `plan_`.
- **product_id** `string | null` _requerido_ — The product the payment was for, prefixed `prod_`.
- **reason** `string` _requerido_ — What the customer says went wrong. Shares the `/disputes` vocabulary, so a case that later becomes a chargeback reports the same complaint. · valores: `fraudulent`, `product_not_received`, `not_as_described`, `product_unacceptable`, `subscription_canceled`
- **refund** `string | null` _requerido_ — Whether money moved and off whose balance: `none`, `merchant`, or `platform` (Whop refunded the customer and the merchant kept the funds). Independent of `outcome` — a case the merchant won can still carry a platform refund. `null` while the case is open, and on older closed cases that predate this being recorded. · valores: `none`, `merchant`, `platform`, `None`
- **response_due_at** `string | null` _requerido_ — When the next response is due, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

- **updated_at** `string` _requerido_ — When the case was last changed, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

**`401`** — Unauthorized

- **error** `object` _requerido_
  - **code** `string` — Machine-readable reason for this specific refusal, such as `bank_warning_not_acknowledged`. Only present when the error carries one.

## `PATCH /setup_intents/{setup_intent_id}/return_url`

**Update setup return URL**

Changes where the buyer lands after completing an off-site step, up until they return. Accepts either a secret key or the setup's own `client_secret`, so the surface that knows the final destination can set it.

`operationId`: `updateReturnUrlSetupIntent` · tags: `Setup Intents` · seguridad: `bearerAuth`

### Parámetros

- **setup_intent_id** (`path`) `string` _requerido_ — The unique identifier of the setup intent.

### Request body — `application/json` (requerido)

- **return_url** `string` _requerido_ — Where the buyer continues after completing an off-site step. Must be an absolute https URL without credentials (http is allowed for localhost), at most 2,048 characters.

### Respuestas

**`200`** — Return URL updated

- **id** `string` _requerido_ — The setup this status describes, prefixed `sint_`.
- **last_setup_error** `SetupLastSetupError | null` _requerido_ — Why the setup ended where it did, or `null` when nothing has failed. Present on `canceled` — a buyer who abandoned carries no code, one refused by the provider does.
  - _uno de:_
    - **SetupLastSetupError**
      - **code** `string | null` _requerido_ — A machine-readable classification of the failure, e.g. `enrollment_declined`. Absent when the buyer simply abandoned the setup.
      - **message** `string | null` _requerido_ — A human-readable explanation of the failure.
    - **null**
- **next_action** `PaymentNextAction | null` _requerido_ — What the buyer must do next while `status` is `requires_action`, otherwise `null`. `type` picks the shape and each variant carries only its own `data`, so switching on `type` gives you exactly that step's payload.
  - _uno de:_
    - **PaymentNextAction**
      - _uno de:_
        - **PaymentNextActionRedirect**
          - **data** `PaymentNextActionRedirectData` _requerido_ — Where to send the buyer.
            - **frame_max_width** `integer | null` _requerido_ — The widest the provider's page lays out usefully, in CSS pixels — cap a frame or dialog presenting it at this width. `null` when the page fills whatever width it is given.
            - **url** `string` _requerido_ — The provider's page for this payment, as an absolute URL — take the buyer there.
          - **render** `string[]` _requerido_
            - `array` de:
              - Where this step can be presented: `inline` inside your own page, `full_page` as a top-level navigation. Pick whichever listed mode suits your surface.
          - **type** `string` _requerido_ — Always `redirect`: send the buyer to `data.url`. The provider hands them back to `return_url` when they are done. · valores: `redirect`
        - **PaymentNextActionDisplayInstructions**
          - **data** `PaymentInstructions` _requerido_ — The instructions. `kind` picks the shape, and the details sit under the key named for it: `voucher`, `qr`, or `bank_transfer`.
            - _uno de:_
              - **PaymentVoucherInstructions**
                - **kind** `string` _requerido_ — Always `voucher`: a code the buyer pays in person, at a convenience store or bank counter. · valores: `voucher`
                - **voucher** `PaymentVoucher` _requerido_ — The voucher to show.
                  - **amount** `Money` — Exactly what the buyer must pay, in the charged currency.
                    - **amount** `string` _requerido_ — The amount in major units, as an exact decimal string — `"10.00"` is ten dollars. A string so no float rounds it in transit.
                    - **currency** `string` _requerido_ — Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code, lowercase.
                    - **decimals** `integer` _requerido_ — How many decimal places the amount CARRIES — the precision the charge itself runs at.
                    - **display_decimals** `integer` _requerido_ — How many decimal places to SHOW. Usually equal to `decimals`, and deliberately not always: COP is charged in centavos but written in whole pesos, so it is `2` and `0`. Format the number in your own locale using this.
                  - **barcode** `string` — The barcode's contents, when the voucher carries one — render it in the symbology named by `barcode_format`.
                  - **barcode_format** `string` — The symbology `barcode` is encoded in, such as `CODE_128`.
                  - **company_name** `string` — Who the payment is made out to.
                  - **document_url** `string` — A hosted page with the complete, printable instructions. If you would rather not render the details yourself, send the buyer here.
                  - **expires_at** `string` — When the voucher stops being payable, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.
                  - **provider_logo** `string` — URL of that network's logo.
                  - **provider_name** `string` — The network the buyer pays at, such as OXXO.
                  - **reference** `string` — The voucher's number — what the buyer reads out or types at the counter to pay.
              - **PaymentQrInstructions**
                - **kind** `string` _requerido_ — Always `qr`: a code the buyer scans with their banking app. · valores: `qr`
                - **qr** `PaymentQr` _requerido_ — The code to show.
                  - **amount** `Money` — Exactly what the buyer must pay, in the charged currency.
                    - **amount** `string` _requerido_ — The amount in major units, as an exact decimal string — `"10.00"` is ten dollars. A string so no float rounds it in transit.
                    - **currency** `string` _requerido_ — Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code, lowercase.
                    - **decimals** `integer` _requerido_ — How many decimal places the amount CARRIES — the precision the charge itself runs at.
                    - **display_decimals** `integer` _requerido_ — How many decimal places to SHOW. Usually equal to `decimals`, and deliberately not always: COP is charged in centavos but written in whole pesos, so it is `2` and `0`. Format the number in your own locale using this.
                  - **document_url** `string` — A hosted page with the complete, printable instructions. If you would rather not render the details yourself, send the buyer here.
                  - **expires_at** `string` — When the code stops being payable, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.
                  - **key** `string` — An account key the buyer can pay to directly (Colombia's Bre-B llave), for apps that take a key instead of a scan.
                  - **qr_code** `string` — The QR code's contents, ready to render as a scannable image — `qr_format` says how it is encoded.
                  - **qr_format** `string` — How `qr_code` is encoded.
              - **PaymentBankTransferInstructions**
                - **bank_transfer** `PaymentBankTransfer` _requerido_ — The account details to show.
                  - **account_number** `string` — The account to send to, in the local scheme's format — `account_number_label` says what to call it.
                  - **account_number_label** `string` — What to call `account_number` when showing it, in the local scheme's own terms — `CLABE` in Mexico, for example.
                  - **amount** `Money` — Exactly what the buyer must send, in the charged currency.
                    - **amount** `string` _requerido_ — The amount in major units, as an exact decimal string — `"10.00"` is ten dollars. A string so no float rounds it in transit.
                    - **currency** `string` _requerido_ — Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code, lowercase.
                    - **decimals** `integer` _requerido_ — How many decimal places the amount CARRIES — the precision the charge itself runs at.
                    - **display_decimals** `integer` _requerido_ — How many decimal places to SHOW. Usually equal to `decimals`, and deliberately not always: COP is charged in centavos but written in whole pesos, so it is `2` and `0`. Format the number in your own locale using this.
                  - **bank_account_type** `string` — The kind of account receiving the transfer, such as a checking account, in the local system's own vocabulary.
                  - **bank_address** `string` — The receiving bank's address.
                  - **bank_branch** `string` — The receiving branch, where the local system routes by branch.
                  - **bank_code** `string` — The receiving bank's code in the local clearing system.
                  - **bank_name** `string` — The receiving bank's name.
                  - **beneficiary_document** `string` — The account holder's tax or identity document number, where the local system needs it to send.
                  - **beneficiary_document_type** `string` — What kind of document `beneficiary_document` is, in the local system's own vocabulary.
                  - **beneficiary_name** `string` — Who the account belongs to — the name the buyer's bank may ask them to confirm.
                  - **document_url** `string` — A hosted page with the complete, printable instructions. If you would rather not render the details yourself, send the buyer here.
                  - **expires_at** `string` — When these details stop being payable, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.
                  - **instructions** `string` — The rail's own step-by-step payment text, when it supplies one.
                  - **reference** `string` — The reference the buyer must attach to the transfer so it can be matched to this payment.
                  - **routing_number** `string` — The receiving bank's routing number for US transfers.
                  - **secondary_account_number** `string` — A second account number, where the rail publishes the same destination in more than one format.
                  - **secondary_account_number_label** `string` — What to call `secondary_account_number` when showing it.
                - **kind** `string` _requerido_ — Always `bank_transfer`: account details the buyer sends money to from their own bank. · valores: `bank_transfer`
          - **render** `string[]` _requerido_
            - `array` de:
              - Where this step can be presented: `inline` inside your own page, `full_page` as a top-level navigation. Pick whichever listed mode suits your surface.
          - **type** `string` _requerido_ — Always `display_instructions`: show the buyer `data` — what to pay, where, and by when. The payment completes once they pay and the rail confirms it, so keep polling `status`. · valores: `display_instructions`
        - **PaymentNextActionAwaitConfirmation**
          - **data** `PaymentNextActionAwaitConfirmationData` _requerido_ — How long the wait can last.
            - **expires_at** `string` _requerido_ — When the confirmation window closes, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. A payment still unconfirmed by then will not succeed — watch `status` for the failed attempt.
          - **render** `string[]` _requerido_
            - `array` de:
              - Where this step can be presented: `inline` inside your own page, `full_page` as a top-level navigation. Pick whichever listed mode suits your surface.
          - **type** `string` _requerido_ — Always `await_confirmation`: nothing to show — the buyer has done their part and the rail settles out of band. Poll `status` until it moves. · valores: `await_confirmation`
    - **null**
- **object** `string` _requerido_ — Always `setup_status`.
- **return_url** `string | null` _requerido_ — Where to send the buyer once the setup reaches a resting state, or `null` to leave them where they are.
- **status** `string` _requerido_ — How far the setup has got. **A 200 means we answered, not that the method was saved — always branch on this.** `requires_action` — the buyer has a step outstanding; see `next_action`. `processing` — the buyer has done their part and the processor is deciding. `succeeded` — the payment method is saved, and only this one means saved. `canceled` — abandoned or refused; see `last_setup_error` to tell which. · valores: `processing`, `succeeded`, `canceled`, `requires_action`

**`400`** — Invalid Parameters

- **error** `object` _requerido_
  - **code** `string` — Machine-readable reason for this specific refusal, such as `bank_warning_not_acknowledged`. Only present when the error carries one.
  - **message** `string` _requerido_ — Human-readable error message.
  - **type** `string` _requerido_ — Machine-readable error code.

**`401`** — Unauthorized

- **error** `object` _requerido_
  - **code** `string` — Machine-readable reason for this specific refusal, such as `bank_warning_not_acknowledged`. Only present when the error carries one.
  - **message** `string` _requerido_ — Human-readable error message.
  - **type** `string` _requerido_ — Machine-readable error code.

**`403`** — Forbidden

- **error** `object` _requerido_
  - **code** `string` — Machine-readable reason for this specific refusal, such as `bank_warning_not_acknowledged`. Only present when the error carries one.
  - **message** `string` _requerido_ — Human-readable error message.
  - **type** `string` _requerido_ — Machine-readable error code.

## `GET /setup_intents/{setup_intent_id}/status`

**Retrieve setup status**

Retrieves how far a setup has got and what the buyer must do next, if anything. Collection runs in the background, so poll this rather than reading the create response. Accepts either a secret key or the setup's own `client_secret`, so the surface collecting the payment method can poll it directly.

`operationId`: `retrieveStatusSetupIntent` · tags: `Setup Intents` · seguridad: `bearerAuth`

### Parámetros

- **setup_intent_id** (`path`) `string` _requerido_ — The unique identifier of the setup intent.

### Respuestas

**`200`** — Setup status retrieved

- **id** `string` _requerido_ — The setup this status describes, prefixed `sint_`.
- **last_setup_error** `SetupLastSetupError | null` _requerido_ — Why the setup ended where it did, or `null` when nothing has failed. Present on `canceled` — a buyer who abandoned carries no code, one refused by the provider does.
  - _uno de:_
    - **SetupLastSetupError**
      - **code** `string | null` _requerido_ — A machine-readable classification of the failure, e.g. `enrollment_declined`. Absent when the buyer simply abandoned the setup.
      - **message** `string | null` _requerido_ — A human-readable explanation of the failure.
    - **null**
- **next_action** `PaymentNextAction | null` _requerido_ — What the buyer must do next while `status` is `requires_action`, otherwise `null`. `type` picks the shape and each variant carries only its own `data`, so switching on `type` gives you exactly that step's payload.
  - _uno de:_
    - **PaymentNextAction**
      - _uno de:_
        - **PaymentNextActionRedirect**
          - **data** `PaymentNextActionRedirectData` _requerido_ — Where to send the buyer.
            - **frame_max_width** `integer | null` _requerido_ — The widest the provider's page lays out usefully, in CSS pixels — cap a frame or dialog presenting it at this width. `null` when the page fills whatever width it is given.
            - **url** `string` _requerido_ — The provider's page for this payment, as an absolute URL — take the buyer there.
          - **render** `string[]` _requerido_
            - `array` de:
              - Where this step can be presented: `inline` inside your own page, `full_page` as a top-level navigation. Pick whichever listed mode suits your surface.
          - **type** `string` _requerido_ — Always `redirect`: send the buyer to `data.url`. The provider hands them back to `return_url` when they are done. · valores: `redirect`
        - **PaymentNextActionDisplayInstructions**
          - **data** `PaymentInstructions` _requerido_ — The instructions. `kind` picks the shape, and the details sit under the key named for it: `voucher`, `qr`, or `bank_transfer`.
            - _uno de:_
              - **PaymentVoucherInstructions**
                - **kind** `string` _requerido_ — Always `voucher`: a code the buyer pays in person, at a convenience store or bank counter. · valores: `voucher`
                - **voucher** `PaymentVoucher` _requerido_ — The voucher to show.
                  - **amount** `Money` — Exactly what the buyer must pay, in the charged currency.
                    - **amount** `string` _requerido_ — The amount in major units, as an exact decimal string — `"10.00"` is ten dollars. A string so no float rounds it in transit.
                    - **currency** `string` _requerido_ — Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code, lowercase.
                    - **decimals** `integer` _requerido_ — How many decimal places the amount CARRIES — the precision the charge itself runs at.
                    - **display_decimals** `integer` _requerido_ — How many decimal places to SHOW. Usually equal to `decimals`, and deliberately not always: COP is charged in centavos but written in whole pesos, so it is `2` and `0`. Format the number in your own locale using this.
                  - **barcode** `string` — The barcode's contents, when the voucher carries one — render it in the symbology named by `barcode_format`.
                  - **barcode_format** `string` — The symbology `barcode` is encoded in, such as `CODE_128`.
                  - **company_name** `string` — Who the payment is made out to.
                  - **document_url** `string` — A hosted page with the complete, printable instructions. If you would rather not render the details yourself, send the buyer here.
                  - **expires_at** `string` — When the voucher stops being payable, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.
                  - **provider_logo** `string` — URL of that network's logo.
                  - **provider_name** `string` — The network the buyer pays at, such as OXXO.
                  - **reference** `string` — The voucher's number — what the buyer reads out or types at the counter to pay.
              - **PaymentQrInstructions**
                - **kind** `string` _requerido_ — Always `qr`: a code the buyer scans with their banking app. · valores: `qr`
                - **qr** `PaymentQr` _requerido_ — The code to show.
                  - **amount** `Money` — Exactly what the buyer must pay, in the charged currency.
                    - **amount** `string` _requerido_ — The amount in major units, as an exact decimal string — `"10.00"` is ten dollars. A string so no float rounds it in transit.
                    - **currency** `string` _requerido_ — Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code, lowercase.
                    - **decimals** `integer` _requerido_ — How many decimal places the amount CARRIES — the precision the charge itself runs at.
                    - **display_decimals** `integer` _requerido_ — How many decimal places to SHOW. Usually equal to `decimals`, and deliberately not always: COP is charged in centavos but written in whole pesos, so it is `2` and `0`. Format the number in your own locale using this.
                  - **document_url** `string` — A hosted page with the complete, printable instructions. If you would rather not render the details yourself, send the buyer here.
                  - **expires_at** `string` — When the code stops being payable, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.
                  - **key** `string` — An account key the buyer can pay to directly (Colombia's Bre-B llave), for apps that take a key instead of a scan.
                  - **qr_code** `string` — The QR code's contents, ready to render as a scannable image — `qr_format` says how it is encoded.
                  - **qr_format** `string` — How `qr_code` is encoded.
              - **PaymentBankTransferInstructions**
                - **bank_transfer** `PaymentBankTransfer` _requerido_ — The account details to show.
                  - **account_number** `string` — The account to send to, in the local scheme's format — `account_number_label` says what to call it.
                  - **account_number_label** `string` — What to call `account_number` when showing it, in the local scheme's own terms — `CLABE` in Mexico, for example.
                  - **amount** `Money` — Exactly what the buyer must send, in the charged currency.
                    - **amount** `string` _requerido_ — The amount in major units, as an exact decimal string — `"10.00"` is ten dollars. A string so no float rounds it in transit.
                    - **currency** `string` _requerido_ — Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code, lowercase.
                    - **decimals** `integer` _requerido_ — How many decimal places the amount CARRIES — the precision the charge itself runs at.
                    - **display_decimals** `integer` _requerido_ — How many decimal places to SHOW. Usually equal to `decimals`, and deliberately not always: COP is charged in centavos but written in whole pesos, so it is `2` and `0`. Format the number in your own locale using this.
                  - **bank_account_type** `string` — The kind of account receiving the transfer, such as a checking account, in the local system's own vocabulary.
                  - **bank_address** `string` — The receiving bank's address.
                  - **bank_branch** `string` — The receiving branch, where the local system routes by branch.
                  - **bank_code** `string` — The receiving bank's code in the local clearing system.
                  - **bank_name** `string` — The receiving bank's name.
                  - **beneficiary_document** `string` — The account holder's tax or identity document number, where the local system needs it to send.
                  - **beneficiary_document_type** `string` — What kind of document `beneficiary_document` is, in the local system's own vocabulary.
                  - **beneficiary_name** `string` — Who the account belongs to — the name the buyer's bank may ask them to confirm.
                  - **document_url** `string` — A hosted page with the complete, printable instructions. If you would rather not render the details yourself, send the buyer here.
                  - **expires_at** `string` — When these details stop being payable, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.
                  - **instructions** `string` — The rail's own step-by-step payment text, when it supplies one.
                  - **reference** `string` — The reference the buyer must attach to the transfer so it can be matched to this payment.
                  - **routing_number** `string` — The receiving bank's routing number for US transfers.
                  - **secondary_account_number** `string` — A second account number, where the rail publishes the same destination in more than one format.
                  - **secondary_account_number_label** `string` — What to call `secondary_account_number` when showing it.
                - **kind** `string` _requerido_ — Always `bank_transfer`: account details the buyer sends money to from their own bank. · valores: `bank_transfer`
          - **render** `string[]` _requerido_
            - `array` de:
              - Where this step can be presented: `inline` inside your own page, `full_page` as a top-level navigation. Pick whichever listed mode suits your surface.
          - **type** `string` _requerido_ — Always `display_instructions`: show the buyer `data` — what to pay, where, and by when. The payment completes once they pay and the rail confirms it, so keep polling `status`. · valores: `display_instructions`
        - **PaymentNextActionAwaitConfirmation**
          - **data** `PaymentNextActionAwaitConfirmationData` _requerido_ — How long the wait can last.
            - **expires_at** `string` _requerido_ — When the confirmation window closes, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. A payment still unconfirmed by then will not succeed — watch `status` for the failed attempt.
          - **render** `string[]` _requerido_
            - `array` de:
              - Where this step can be presented: `inline` inside your own page, `full_page` as a top-level navigation. Pick whichever listed mode suits your surface.
          - **type** `string` _requerido_ — Always `await_confirmation`: nothing to show — the buyer has done their part and the rail settles out of band. Poll `status` until it moves. · valores: `await_confirmation`
    - **null**
- **object** `string` _requerido_ — Always `setup_status`.
- **return_url** `string | null` _requerido_ — Where to send the buyer once the setup reaches a resting state, or `null` to leave them where they are.
- **status** `string` _requerido_ — How far the setup has got. **A 200 means we answered, not that the method was saved — always branch on this.** `requires_action` — the buyer has a step outstanding; see `next_action`. `processing` — the buyer has done their part and the processor is deciding. `succeeded` — the payment method is saved, and only this one means saved. `canceled` — abandoned or refused; see `last_setup_error` to tell which. · valores: `processing`, `succeeded`, `canceled`, `requires_action`

**`401`** — Unauthorized

- **error** `object` _requerido_
  - **code** `string` — Machine-readable reason for this specific refusal, such as `bank_warning_not_acknowledged`. Only present when the error carries one.
  - **message** `string` _requerido_ — Human-readable error message.
  - **type** `string` _requerido_ — Machine-readable error code.

**`403`** — Forbidden

- **error** `object` _requerido_
  - **code** `string` — Machine-readable reason for this specific refusal, such as `bank_warning_not_acknowledged`. Only present when the error carries one.
  - **message** `string` _requerido_ — Human-readable error message.

## `GET /shipments`

**List Shipments**

Returns a paginated list of shipments for an account.

`operationId`: `listShipments` · tags: `Shipments` · seguridad: `bearerAuth`

### Parámetros

- **Api-Version-Date** (`header`) `string` — Pins the request to a dated API version.
- **account_id** (`query`) `string` — The account to list shipments for. Defaults to the acting account.
- **status** (`query`) `string` — Filter to shipments with this delivery status. · valores: `unknown`, `pre_transit`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `available_for_pickup`, `return_to_sender`, `failure`, `cancelled`, `error`
- **payment_id** (`query`) `string[]` — Only shipments fulfilling these payments, each prefixed `pay_`. Repeat the parameter to pass several, up to 100 per request — one paginated list covers all of them.
- **created_before** (`query`) `string` — Return shipments created before this ISO 8601 timestamp.
- **created_after** (`query`) `string` — Return shipments created after this ISO 8601 timestamp.
- **order** (`query`) `string` — The field to sort by. · valores: `created_at`
- **direction** (`query`) `string` — The sort direction. · valores: `asc`, `desc`
- **first** (`query`) `integer` — The number of shipments to return.
- **after** (`query`) `string` — A cursor; returns shipments after this position.
- **last** (`query`) `integer` — The number of shipments to return from the end of the range.
- **before** (`query`) `string` — A cursor; returns shipments before this position.

**`200`** — excludes the created_after boundary row

  - `array` de:

        - **timestamp** `string | null` _requerido_ — When the carrier recorded the scan, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. Null when the carrier sent no scan time.
    - **created_at** `string` _requerido_ — The datetime the shipment was created (ISO 8601).
    - **id** `string` _requerido_ — Shipment ID, prefixed `ship_`.
    - **payment_id** `string` _requerido_ — The payment this shipment fulfills, prefixed `pay_`.
    - **status** `string` _requerido_ — The current delivery status of this shipment. · valores: `unknown`, `pre_transit`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `available_for_pickup`, `return_to_sender`, `failure`, `cancelled`, `error`
    - **tracking_number** `string` _requerido_ — The carrier-assigned tracking number used to look up shipment progress.
    - **tracking_url** `string` _requerido_ — A customer-facing URL to track this shipment's progress.
    - **updated_at** `string` _requerido_ — The datetime the shipment was last updated (ISO 8601).
- **page_info** `object` _requerido_
  - **end_cursor** `string | null` _requerido_
  - **has_next_page** `boolean` _requerido_
  - **has_previous_page** `boolean` _requerido_

## `POST /social_accounts/connect`

- **platform** `string` _requerido_ — The platform to connect the social account on. Use `meta_business` to connect Meta Business assets, which is how Facebook Pages and Instagram accounts are connected — there is no separate `instagram` value. Use `tiktok` for TikTok accounts. · valores: `meta_business`, `tiktok`
- **redirect_url** `string` — The Whop URL the user is sent to after Whop has processed the platform's OAuth callback. This is not the OAuth `redirect_uri` — the returned `authorize_url` always points at Whop's own callback endpoint, so expect the `redirect_uri` inside it to differ from this value.
- **scopes** `string[]` — Capabilities to grant for the connected social account. `advertise` is required for both `meta_business` and `tiktok` connections — it is not conditional on whether you intend to run ads, and omitting it fails the request.

## `GET /social_accounts/{id}/lead_forms`

**List Social Account Lead Forms**

Lists the active lead (instant) forms that already exist on a connected Facebook page, so an ad can reuse one as its `lead_gen_form_id` instead of authoring a new form. Every active form comes back in a single response — the list is not paginated.

`operationId`: `listSocialAccountLeadForms` · tags: `Social Accounts` · seguridad: `bearerAuth`

### Parámetros

- **Api-Version-Date** (`header`) `string` — Pins the request to a dated API version.
- **id** (`path`) `string` _requerido_ — The social account (a sacc_ identifier) whose lead forms to list.
- **account_id** (`query`) `string` _requerido_ — The Account (a biz_ identifier) the social account is connected to.

### Respuestas

**`200`** — lead forms listed

- **data** `SocialAccountLeadForm[]` _requerido_
  - `array` de:
    - **completion** `AdLeadFormCompletion | null` _requerido_ — Screen shown after the form is submitted. `null` when the form has none.
      - _uno de:_
        - **AdLeadFormCompletion**
          - **button_text** `string | null` _requerido_ — Text of the follow-up button.
          - **description** `string | null` _requerido_ — Body text under the headline.
          - **headline** `string | null` _requerido_ — Headline of the completion screen.
          - **url** `string | null` _requerido_ — Website the follow-up button opens. `null` when the screen has no button.
        - **null**
    - **created_at** `string | null` _requerido_ — When the form was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.
    - **disclaimer** `AdLeadFormDisclaimer | null` _requerido_ — Custom consent disclaimer shown before submission. `null` when the form has none.
      - _uno de:_
        - **AdLeadFormDisclaimer**
          - **body** `string | null` _requerido_ — Disclaimer text.
          - **checkboxes** `AdLeadFormDisclaimerCheckbox[]` _requerido_
            - `array` de:
              - **checked_by_default** `boolean | null` _requerido_ — Whether the checkbox starts ticked.
              - **key** `string | null` _requerido_ — Stable identifier consent responses are stored under.
              - **required** `boolean | null` _requerido_ — Whether the checkbox must be ticked to submit the form.
              - **text** `string` _requerido_ — Consent text next to the checkbox.
          - **title** `string | null` _requerido_ — Disclaimer title.
        - **null**
    - **form_type** `string` _requerido_ — `more_volume` is quickest to submit; `higher_intent` adds a confirmation step before submission. · valores: `more_volume`, `higher_intent`
    - **id** `string` _requerido_ — The ad platform's identifier for the form. Use it as lead_gen_form_id on an ad to reuse the form.
    - **intro** `AdLeadFormIntro | null` _requerido_ — Intro screen shown before the questions. `null` when the form has none.
      - _uno de:_
        - **AdLeadFormIntro**
          - **description** `string | null` _requerido_ — Body text under the headline.
          - **headline** `string | null` _requerido_ — Headline of the intro screen.
        - **null**
    - **locale** `string | null` _requerido_ — Language the form is shown in, such as en_US.
    - **name** `string | null` _requerido_ — Advertiser-facing form name.
    - **privacy_policy_link_text** `string | null` _requerido_ — Custom link text for the privacy policy. `null` when the default is used.
    - **privacy_policy_url** `string | null` _requerido_ — Privacy policy URL configured on the form.
    - **question_labels** `string[]` _requerido_
      - `array` de:
        - Labels of the questions the form asks, for preview.
    - **questions** `AdLeadFormQuestion[]` _requerido_
      - `array` de:
        - **format** `string` — Answer format for `custom` questions: `short_answer`, `multiple_choice`, or `appointment`. Absent otherwise.
        - **label** `string` — Question text for `custom` questions. Absent for standard prefill questions.
        - **options** `AdLeadFormQuestionOption[]`
          - `array` de:
            - **key** `string | null` — Stable identifier the choice's answers are stored under. Absent for simple choices.
            - **logic** `AdLeadFormOptionLogic` — Where the form goes when this choice is selected. Absent when the form just continues to the next question.
              - **action** `string` _requerido_ — What happens when the choice is selected. · valores: `go_to_question`, `submit_form`, `close_form`
              - **target_end_page_index** `number` — Zero-based index of the ending screen to jump to.
              - **target_question_index** `number` — Zero-based index of the question to jump to, for `go_to_question`.
            - **value** `string` _requerido_ — Choice text shown to the person.
        - **type** `string` _requerido_ — Question type: a standard prefill type such as `email`, `phone`, or `full_name`, or `custom` for your own question.

**`400`** — Invalid Parameters

- **error** `object` _requerido_
  - **code** `string` — Machine-readable reason for this specific refusal, such as `bank_warning_not_acknowledged`. Only present when the error carries one.

  - **type** `string` _requerido_ — Machine-readable error code.

## `GET /social_accounts/{id}/posts`

**List Social Account Posts**

Lists the existing posts of a connected Facebook page, Instagram account, or TikTok account.

`operationId`: `listSocialAccountPosts` · tags: `Social Accounts` · seguridad: `bearerAuth`

### Parámetros

- **Api-Version-Date** (`header`) `string` — Pins the request to a dated API version.
- **id** (`path`) `string` _requerido_ — The social account (a sacc_ identifier) whose posts to list.
- **account_id** (`query`) `string` _requerido_ — The Account (a biz_ identifier) the social account is connected to.
- **post_id** (`query`) `string` — Return only the single post with this platform id, instead of the full list.
- **first** (`query`) `integer` — The number of posts to return. · default: `20`
- **after** (`query`) `string` — Cursor to fetch the page after (from page_info.end_cursor).

### Respuestas

**`200`** — single post returned when post_id is given

- **data** `SocialAccountPost[]` _requerido_
  - `array` de:
    - **call_to_action** `string | null` _requerido_ — The post's call-to-action button, for example shop_now (Facebook only; null for Instagram and TikTok). · valores: `learn_more`, `shop_now`, `sign_up`, `subscribe`, `get_started`, `book_now`, `apply_now`, `contact_us`, `download`, `order_now`, `buy_now`, `get_quote`, `message_page`, `whatsapp_message`, `instagram_message`, `call_now`, `get_directions`, `send_updates`, `get_offer`, `watch_more`, `listen_now`, `play_game`, `open_link`, `no_button` …
    - **destination_url** `string | null` _requerido_ — The URL the post's call-to-action drives to (Facebook only; null for Instagram and TikTok).
    - **embed_url** `string | null` _requerido_ — An iframe-embeddable URL for previewing the post inline (the platform's player or post embed). For TikTok this is the only preview, since media_url is null; for Facebook and Instagram it supplements media_url. Null when no public embed is available.
    - **id** `string` _requerido_ — The platform's own identifier for the post or media. Use it to reference the post on an ad.
    - **media_url** `string | null` _requerido_ — The URL of the post's media — the image for image posts, the playable video file for video posts. Null for TikTok, which exposes no raw file (use embed_url). Meta URLs are signed and expire after roughly 24 hours, so don't store them.
    - **restrictions** `string[]` _requerido_
      - `array` de:
        - Ways this post can't be used on an ad. `lead_form_ineligible`: post can't be used in lead form ads. `promotion_ineligible`: the platform won't promote this post at all — always present when that's true, alongside a reason code when one is identified. `copyrighted_music`: post uses music the platform does not allow for ads. `messenger_destination`, `instagram_destination`, `whatsapp_destination`: the post's own button opens that chat app, so the post can only run in an ad group that sends people to the same one — always accompanied by `lead_form_ineligible`. Empty when the post has no restrictions.
    - **thumbnail_url** `string | null` _requerido_ — Poster image for video posts (always set for TikTok, which is video-only); null for image posts, where media_url is already the image.
- **page_info** `object` _requerido_
  - **end_cursor** `string` _requerido_
  - **has_next_page** `boolean` _requerido_

**`400`** — Invalid Parameters

- **error** `object` _requerido_
  - **code** `string` — Machine-readable reason for this specific refusal, such as `bank_warning_not_acknowledged`. Only present when the error carries one.
  - **message** `string` _requerido_ — Human-readable error message.
  - **type** `string` _requerido_ — Machine-readable error code.

**`401`** — Unauthorized

- **error** `object` _requerido_

    - **name** `string` _requerido_ — Human-readable display name for the metric.
    - **properties** `string[]` _requerido_ — The properties you can use with this metric — pass one as a filter (property=value) to narrow the series, or as breakdown_by=property to split it.
      - `array` de:
    - **unit** `string` _requerido_ — How to read the metric's values: count is an integer, currency is a decimal amount, and percent is a number where 1.6 means 1.6%. · valores: `count`, `currency`, `percent`
    - **windows** `string[]` — Snapshot metrics only: the trailing windows you can pass as snapshot_window, for example 30d. Absent on live metrics, which use from/to instead.
      - `array` de:

**`401`** — Unauthorized

- **error** `object` _requerido_
  - **code** `string` — Machine-readable reason for this specific refusal, such as `bank_warning_not_acknowledged`. Only present when the error carries one.
  - **message** `string` _requerido_ — Human-readable error message.
  - **type** `string` _requerido_ — Machine-readable error code.
